name: Language servers
responsibility: Asks the language server of a file's language where a name the file uses is defined, and what the definition declares, for one pass of the code check
description: TASK-367.13 to TASK-367.16, TASK-433 and ADR 0046. One pass starts the server of each language once per project on its first question: the checkout, for Swift the package that holds the file, for C, C++ and Objective-C the directory of its compile_commands.json. It speaks JSON-RPC over the child's stdio, asks textDocument/definition at the last name of a use on its line, and textDocument/documentSymbol once per file to tell code that runs from a member of a type. A language's row in languages.ts says what its server needs beyond that: pyright is told the checkout's .venv or venv; csharp-ls the solution nearest the root; sourcekit-lsp starts normally, builds and prepares its Swift package through background indexing, is asked workspace/synchronize with index true once and has each file opened; clangd has each file opened, finds its compile_commands.json where it would, keeps its own index where an editor's clangd does, and is asked once that index has ended. The command comes from server-command.ts. Every language but TypeScript runs only what the agent in that repository set on the checkout's registration (repo language-server), with the environment of the Archboard server and nothing added; if none is configured, the pass says so once for the checkout and the language, naming the command that configures one. TypeScript runs the native tsc --lsp of the checkout's own typescript package from version 7 on, with its native program, both inside the checkout, else Archboard's own. Every server has stopped before the pass returns: shutdown and exit, then a kill of its process group, or a kill at once when the pass is cancelled. A server that fails is said once for its checkout, and so is a project it cannot answer about, for which no server starts: a C file with no compile_commands.json.
